title: Correlation and Branching Mechanisms in the Quantum-to-Classical Transition of Interacting Systems
abstract: We analyze the quantum-to-classical transition of interacting systems from the viewpoint of reduced dynamical closure. Bohmian trajectories are used as a diagnostic of the probability flow generated by the full wavefunction, rather than as an alternative set of quantum predictions. A closed classical or semiclassical description of a retained coordinate can emerge either because interaction-induced correlations are suppressed or because the observable of interest is insensitive to the correlations that remain. Three models are used to isolate distinct mechanisms. In a hard-core collision, the leading tail of a broad relative-coordinate wave packet reaches the boundary before its center and generates spatial nonseparability through reflection and interference. In the Rabi model, the mixed quantum-classical Ehrenfest approximation fails when spin-position covariances prevent the spin dynamics from being determined solely by the mean oscillator coordinate. In an internal-state-dependent force model, the total mean position obeys an exact Ehrenfest equation, while the wavefunction separates into branch-resolved pointer components; mean classicality therefore does not imply branch-level classicality. These examples show that the quantum-to-classical transition of interacting systems is controlled not only by wave-packet localization but also by whether and how interaction-induced correlations enter the reduced equations of motion.
summary: This work rigorously examines the quantum-to-classical transition in interacting systems using Bohmian mechanics as a diagnostic tool. It demonstrates that the emergence of classical behavior depends sensitively on interaction-induced correlations, showing that mean classicality does not guarantee full quantum-level classicality. The analysis uses hard-core, Rabi, and ISDF models to map out these distinct correlation mechanisms.
main_problem: The paper analyzes the quantum-to-classical transition in interacting quantum systems, focusing on whether the reduced dynamics for a selected coordinate can be described by a closed classical or semiclassical equation.
main_result: The transition is controlled not only by wave-packet localization but critically by how interaction-induced correlations enter the reduced equations of motion, leading to failures in simple mean-field approximations.
method: The study uses Bohmian trajectories as a diagnostic tool to track probability flow and compares mean-level, distributional, and branch-level notions of classicality across three distinct physical models.
model_or_system: Three models are investigated: a hard-core collision of two particles, the Rabi model (spin-position coupling), and an internal-state-dependent force (ISDF) model. These systems explore how correlations manifest during the transition.
key_observables: Linear Entropy ($S_L(t)$), spin-position covariances, and the comparison between Bohmian ensemble averages and classical/Ehrenfest approximations.
important_parameters: Initial Gaussian width ($\sigma$), coupling strengths ($g_R$), and the fixed scaling parameter $\kappa = m\sigma^2$.
main_assumptions: Bohmian trajectories are used diagnostically, not as alternative predictions; the analysis often relies on fixed scaling sequences ($\kappa$ fixed) to isolate localization effects.
figures_summary: Figures compare Bohmian ensemble averages to classical trajectories for hard-core motion and show the evolution of local spinor weights and closure errors ($\xi_{	ext{cov}}$) for the Rabi model and ISDF model.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes three distinct physical models (hard-core, Rabi, ISDF) to isolate specific mechanisms—such as boundary reflections, covariance failure, or branch separation—that govern the breakdown of simple classical approximations.
why_interesting: It provides a detailed, diagnostic framework for understanding when and why mean-field or semiclassical approximations fail in interacting quantum systems, which is crucial for modeling complex quantum dynamics.

figures.caption: FIG. 1: Trajectories of two distinguishable equal-mass particles with a hard-core interaction. Panels (a)-(d) compare the Bohmian ensemble averages, shown by solid lines, with the corresponding classical elastic-collision trajectories, shown by dashed lines. The initial Gaussian widths are σ = 0.15, 0.20, 0.25, and 0.50, while mσ2 = 0.0625. The velocities are fixed at v1 = −1 and v2 = 0; therefore m = 0.0625/σ2 and pn = mvn vary from panel to panel. The initial positions are x1,0 = 4, and x2,0 = 0. Blue and red curves denote particles 1 and 2, respectively. The vertical black dashed line marks the common classical collision time tc = 4. Each Bohmian average is computed from 300 realizations.

FIG. 2: Two-particle probability density and the linear entropy for the hard-core interaction. Panel (a) shows a snapshot of |Ψ(x1, x2, t)|2 at t = 2 for σ = 0.25, m = 1. The remaining parameters are those of in Fig. 1. Panel (b) shows the linear entropy, cf. Eq. (24), for the hard-core collision, corresponding to the trajectory calculations in Fig. 1. Red, brown, orange and blue curves correspond to σ = 0.15, 0.20, 0.25 and 0.5, respectively, with mσ2 = 0.0625 fixed. The same fixed velocities, v1 = −1, v2 = 0, and common collision time tc = 4 (marked by the vertical black dashed line) are used as in Fig. 1.

FIG. 3: Oscillator trajectories in the Rabi model. Panels (a)–(d) compare the average Bohmian trajectory (red solid lines), the Born expectation value (black dashed lines), and the mixed quantum-classical Ehrenfest trajectory (blue solid lines) for initial wave-packet widths σ = 0.15, 0.20, 0.25, and 0.50, with mσ2 = 0.0625 fixed. The initial conditions are x0 = 2 and v0 = −1 (p0 = mv0 varies) and the up state | ↑⟩is populated. The Bohmian average is obtained from 300 realizations. We use units with ℏ= ω = 1. Other parameters are Ω= 1 and gR = 0.25.

FIG. 4: Spin populations in the Rabi model for the same parameters as in Fig. 3. Blue and red curves denote the two spin components | ↑⟩, | ↓⟩, respectively. Solid curves are obtained from the full quantum calculation (Born expectation), while dashed curves correspond to the mixed quantum-classical Ehrenfest approximation.

FIG. 5: Dimensionless covariance-induced closure-error measure, cf. Eq. (54), for the Rabi-model calculations in Figs. 3 and 4. Red, brown, orange and blue lines correspond to σ = 0.15, 0.2, 0.25 and 0.5, along the fixed-mσ2, fixed-initial-velocity sequence.
